skill.name: twscrape
skill.description: Use twscrape to collect publicly accessible Twitter/X posts, profiles, conversations, and trends with asynchronous Python workflows.
skill.summary: Guidance for using twscrape to collect and analyze public Twitter/X data with Python.
skill.author: 2025Emma

security_audit.summary: Most static alerts are benign documentation examples: placeholder proxies, local file exports, local SQLite paths, and a disclosed upstream installation URL. Manual review found no prompt injection or credential exfiltration. The skill does, however, explicitly describe account rotation to bypass platform limits, which can enable policy-evasive collection.

remediation.issue: The documentation frames account rotation as a way to bypass Twitter/X API limitations.
remediation.suggestion: Replace bypass language with authorized research guidance, require compliance with platform terms, and recommend conservative request limits.

remediation.issue: Examples show account credentials and cookies near source code.
remediation.suggestion: State clearly that users must load secrets from a secure secret manager or environment configuration and must not commit them.

remediation.issue: Examples export collected data to local JSON files.
remediation.suggestion: Add guidance to minimize collection, protect exports with restrictive permissions, and delete data when it is no longer needed.

finding_verdicts.reason: The URL uses the reserved proxy.example.com placeholder and illustrative credentials. It does not direct traffic to an operational endpoint.
127.0.0.1 is the loopback address in an example proxy configuration. It does not contact an external host.
The SOCKS proxy example targets localhost and uses placeholder credentials. Proxy support is documented functionality, not evidence of covert routing.
The code explicitly writes a caller-provided export file as part of a JSON data-export example. It has no hidden path or persistence behavior.
The code writes collected results to the clearly named local results.json file. This is an expected, visible export operation.
my_data.db is a local application database path in a complete workflow example. A SQLite filename alone does not show secret collection or disclosure.
The comparison checks a tweet identifier while iterating search results. It does not inspect the host, network, or operating system.
The comparison stops search iteration when tweet identifiers pass the requested target. It is application control flow, not system reconnaissance.
The URL is the named upstream GitHub repository used for an optional development installation. It is disclosed directly and contains no credentials.
The documentation explains the default local accounts.db location. It does not expose database contents or transmit them.
The custom database path is a local configuration example. It provides no evidence of sensitive-data access beyond the user-selected database.
The CLI example passes a user-chosen local database path. It does not reveal database records or perform network transfer.
Manual review shows a normal Markdown heading at line 1 and no prompt-injection text. The missing frontmatter is a metadata-format issue, not a security threat.

content.value_statement: Collecting public Twitter/X data can require many asynchronous requests and careful result handling. This skill provides documented twscrape workflows for research, export, and basic analysis.
actual_capabilities: Search public Twitter/X posts with query filters and result limits.
Retrieve public profiles, posts, replies, media, followers, and following lists.
Use asynchronous workflows to process multiple public accounts or queries.
Export retrieved profiles and posts to a local JSON file.
Configure a local SQLite database for twscrape account state.
Document proxy configuration and error-handling patterns.
limitations: Requires valid user-controlled access to Twitter/X and network connectivity.
May be restricted by Twitter/X terms, rate limits, account status, and regional access.
Does not provide official Twitter/X API access or guarantee complete results.
Users are responsible for authorization, privacy, and secure handling of account credentials.

use_cases.title: Track public topic discussions
use_cases.description: Search public posts about a defined topic and summarize recurring themes over a limited period.

use_cases.title: Analyze a public brand presence
use_cases.description: Retrieve public posts and replies from a known account for a bounded communications review.

use_cases.title: Export a small public dataset
use_cases.description: Collect a limited set of public posts and save it locally for approved offline analysis.

prompt_templates.title: Start a public post search
prompt_templates.prompt: Show me a minimal asynchronous Python example that searches public Twitter/X posts for a topic, limits results to 20, and prints author and text.

prompt_templates.title: Retrieve a public profile
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me retrieve a public Twitter/X profile by username and list up to 20 recent public posts. Include error handling.

prompt_templates.title: Export approved research data
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a workflow that collects a limited set of public posts from one account and exports only necessary fields to a local JSON file.

prompt_templates.title: Plan compliant batch collection
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a conservative asynchronous collection plan for approved public Twitter/X research. Include rate limits, minimal data fields, retries, and secure credential handling.

output_examples.input: Search public posts about Python with a limit of 20.
output: A list of up to 20 public posts with author names and text.
A reminder to respect platform rules and collection limits.

output_examples.input: Export recent public posts from one approved account.
output: A workflow that retrieves the account and a bounded post set.
A local JSON export containing selected public fields.
Guidance to protect or delete the export when analysis ends.

best_practices: Collect only public data needed for a defined, authorized purpose.
Use conservative limits and respect Twitter/X terms, rate limits, and privacy obligations.
Store account credentials, cookies, databases, and exports securely outside source control.
anti_patterns: Do not use account rotation or proxies to evade platform restrictions or enforcement.
Do not collect sensitive personal data or build datasets without a lawful purpose.
Do not place passwords, cookies, or exported personal data in prompts, code, or repositories.

faq.question: What does this skill help me do?
faq.answer: It documents twscrape workflows for retrieving and analyzing publicly accessible Twitter/X data with Python.

faq.question: Does it provide official Twitter/X API access?
faq.answer: No. It describes a third-party library and does not provide official API credentials or access.

faq.question: Can I use it for large-scale collection?
faq.answer: Use only bounded, authorized collection that complies with platform rules, applicable law, and privacy requirements.

faq.question: How should I store credentials and cookies?
faq.answer: Use a secure secret manager or protected environment configuration. Never commit them to source control.

faq.question: Where are exports and account state stored?
faq.answer: Examples write local JSON files and use a local SQLite database path. Protect these files with appropriate permissions.

faq.question: Will every query return complete results?
faq.answer: No. Results can be limited by account status, rate limits, platform behavior, query syntax, and network conditions.
